passages.text: After these things had been accomplished, the leaders approached me and said, “The people of Israel, including the priests and Levites, have not kept themselves separate from the surrounding peoples whose abominations are like those of the Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Jebusites, Ammonites, Moabites, Egyptians, and Amorites.
passages.sermon:
The leaders came to me after these things were finished.
They spoke to me.
They said the people of Israel have not separated themselves from the peoples of the land.
The priests have not separated themselves.
The Levites have not separated themselves.
The peoples of the land do abominations.
These abominations are like those of the Canaanites.
They are like those of the Hittites.
They are like those of the Perizzites.
They are like those of the Jebusites.
They are like those of the Ammonites.
They are like those of the Moabites.
They are like those of the Egyptians.
They are like those of the Amorites.
passages.original: וּכְכַלּ֣וֹת אֵ֗לֶּה נִגְּשׁ֨וּ אֵלַ֤י הַשָּׂרִים֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹֽא־ נִבְדְּל֞וּ הָעָ֤ם יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וְהַכֹּהֲנִ֣ים וְהַלְוִיִּ֔ם מֵעַמֵּ֖י הָאֲרָצ֑וֹת כְּ֠תוֹעֲבֹֽתֵיהֶם לַכְּנַעֲנִ֨י הַחִתִּ֜י הַפְּרִזִּ֣י הַיְבוּסִ֗י הָֽעַמֹּנִי֙ הַמֹּ֣אָבִ֔י הַמִּצְרִ֖י וְהָאֱמֹרִֽי׃

passages.text: Indeed, the Israelites have taken some of their daughters as wives for themselves and their sons, so that the holy seed has been mixed with the people of the land. And the leaders and officials have taken the lead in this unfaithfulness!”
passages.sermon:
The Israelites are God’s chosen people.
The Israelites have taken daughters from the surrounding peoples as wives.
They have given these women to themselves and to their sons.
The holy people have mixed with the peoples of the land.
The leaders and officials began this unfaithfulness first.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ נָשְׂא֣וּ מִבְּנֹֽתֵיהֶ֗ם לָהֶם֙ וְלִבְנֵיהֶ֔ם וְהִתְעָֽרְבוּ֙ זֶ֣רַע הַקֹּ֔דֶשׁ בְּעַמֵּ֖י הָאֲרָצ֑וֹת וְיַ֧ד הַשָּׂרִ֣ים וְהַסְּגָנִ֗ים הָֽיְתָ֛ה בַּמַּ֥עַל הַזֶּ֖ה רִאשׁוֹנָֽה׃ס

passages.text: When I heard this report, I tore my tunic and cloak, pulled out some hair from my head and beard, and sat down in horror.
passages.sermon:
Ezra was a leader of Israel.
He heard a report about the people's unfaithfulness.
I heard this report.
I tore my tunic.
I tore my cloak.
I pulled out some hair from my head.
I pulled out some hair from my beard.
I sat down in horror.
passages.original: וּכְשָׁמְעִי֙ אֶת־ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה קָרַ֥עְתִּי אֶת־ בִּגְדִ֖י וּמְעִילִ֑י וָאֶמְרְטָ֞ה מִשְּׂעַ֤ר רֹאשִׁי֙ וּזְקָנִ֔י וָאֵשְׁבָ֖ה מְשׁוֹמֵֽם׃

passages.text: Then everyone who trembled at the words of the God of Israel gathered around me because of the unfaithfulness of the exiles, while I sat there in horror until the evening offering.
passages.sermon:
Ezra was a priest and scribe in Israel.
Ezra heard about the unfaithfulness of the exiles.
The exiles had married foreign women and mixed the holy people with the nations.
Everyone who feared the words of the God of Israel gathered around Ezra.
They gathered because of the unfaithfulness of the exiles.
Ezra sat in shock and horror.
He remained sitting until the evening offering.
passages.original: וְאֵלַ֣י יֵאָסְפ֗וּ כֹּ֤ל חָרֵד֙ בְּדִבְרֵ֣י אֱלֹהֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל עַ֖ל מַ֣עַל הַגּוֹלָ֑ה וַאֲנִי֙ יֹשֵׁ֣ב מְשׁוֹמֵ֔ם עַ֖ד לְמִנְחַ֥ת הָעָֽרֶב׃

passages.text: At the evening offering, I got up from my humiliation with my tunic and cloak torn, and I fell on my knees, spread out my hands to the LORD my God, and said: “O my God, I am ashamed and embarrassed to lift up my face to You, my God, because our iniquities are higher than our heads, and our guilt has reached the heavens.
passages.sermon:
Ezra was a priest and scribe in Israel.
Ezra led the people after their return from exile.
At the time of the evening offering, I stood up.
I had been sitting in humiliation.
My tunic and my cloak were torn.
I knelt down on my knees.
I spread out my hands to the LORD my God.
I spoke to God.
I said, “My God, I am ashamed.
I am embarrassed to lift my face to You, my God.
Our sins are very many.
Our sins rise above our heads.
Our guilt is very great.
Our guilt reaches up to the heavens.”
passages.original: וּבְמִנְחַ֣ת הָעֶ֗רֶב קַ֚מְתִּי מִתַּֽעֲנִיתִ֔י וּבְקָרְעִ֥י בִגְדִ֖י וּמְעִילִ֑י וָֽאֶכְרְעָה֙ עַל־ בִּרְכַּ֔י וָאֶפְרְשָׂ֥ה כַפַּ֖י אֶל־ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהָֽי׃ וָאֹמְרָ֗ה אֱלֹהַי֙ בֹּ֣שְׁתִּי וְנִכְלַ֔מְתִּי לְהָרִ֧ים אֱלֹהַ֛י פָּנַ֖י אֵלֶ֑יךָ כִּ֣י עֲוֺנֹתֵ֤ינוּ רָבוּ֙ לְמַ֣עְלָה רֹּ֔אשׁ וְאַשְׁמָתֵ֥נוּ גָדְלָ֖ה עַ֥ד לַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃

passages.text: From the days of our fathers to this day, our guilt has been great. Because of our iniquities, we and our kings and priests have been delivered into the hands of the kings of the earth and put to the sword and captivity, to pillage and humiliation, as we are this day.
passages.sermon:
We are the people of Israel.
Our guilt has been great.
This guilt has lasted from the days of our fathers until today.
We have sinned.
Because of our sins, God has punished us.
God has given us, our kings, and our priests into the hands of foreign kings.
These kings have ruled over many lands.
They have attacked us with the sword.
They have taken us captive.
They have stolen our possessions.
They have brought us shame and humiliation.
We still suffer these things today.
passages.original: מִימֵ֣י אֲבֹתֵ֗ינוּ אֲנַ֙חְנוּ֙ בְּאַשְׁמָ֣ה גְדֹלָ֔ה עַ֖ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה וּבַעֲוֺנֹתֵ֡ינוּ נִתַּ֡נּוּ אֲנַחְנוּ֩ מְלָכֵ֨ינוּ כֹהֲנֵ֜ינוּ בְּיַ֣ד׀ מַלְכֵ֣י הָאֲרָצ֗וֹת בַּחֶ֜רֶב בַּשְּׁבִ֧י וּבַבִּזָּ֛ה וּבְבֹ֥שֶׁת פָּנִ֖ים כְּהַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: But now, for a brief moment, grace has come from the LORD our God to preserve for us a remnant and to give us a stake in His holy place. Even in our bondage, our God has given us new life and light to our eyes.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is our God.
He has shown us grace.
This grace has come for a brief moment.
God has preserved a remnant for us.
He has given us a place in His holy place.
We are still in bondage.
Even so, our God has given us new life.
He has given light to our eyes.
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֡ה כִּמְעַט־ רֶגַע֩ הָיְתָ֨ה תְחִנָּ֜ה מֵאֵ֣ת׀ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ לְהַשְׁאִ֥יר לָ֙נוּ֙ פְּלֵיטָ֔ה וְלָתֶת־ לָ֥נוּ יָתֵ֖ד בִּמְק֣וֹם קָדְשׁ֑וֹ לְהָאִ֤יר עֵינֵ֙ינוּ֙ אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ וּלְתִתֵּ֛נוּ מִֽחְיָ֥ה מְעַ֖ט בְּעַבְדֻתֵֽנוּ׃

passages.text: Though we are slaves, our God has not forsaken us in our bondage, but He has extended to us grace in the sight of the kings of Persia, giving us new life to rebuild the house of our God and repair its ruins, and giving us a wall of protection in Judah and Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
We are slaves.
We live in bondage.
God is our God.
God has not forsaken us.
God showed us grace.
God moved the kings of Persia to show us favor.
God gave us new life.
God allowed us to rebuild the house of our God.
God let us repair its ruins.
God gave us a wall of protection.
God protected us in Judah and Jerusalem.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ עֲבָדִ֣ים אֲנַ֔חְנוּ וּבְעַבְדֻ֔תֵנוּ לֹ֥א עֲזָבָ֖נוּ אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ וַֽיַּט־ עָלֵ֣ינוּ חֶ֡סֶד לִפְנֵי֩ מַלְכֵ֨י פָרַ֜ס לָֽתֶת־ לָ֣נוּ מִֽחְיָ֗ה לְרוֹמֵ֞ם אֶת־ בֵּ֤ית אֱלֹהֵ֙ינוּ֙ וּלְהַעֲמִ֣יד אֶת־ חָרְבֹתָ֔יו וְלָֽתֶת־ לָ֣נוּ גָדֵ֔ר בִּֽיהוּדָ֖ה וּבִירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃ס

passages.text: And now, our God, what can we say after this? For we have forsaken the commandments that You gave through Your servants the prophets, saying: ‘The land that you are entering to possess is a land polluted by the impurity of its peoples and the abominations with which they have filled it from end to end.
passages.sermon:
God is our God.
We have sinned.
We have left Your commandments.
You gave these commandments through Your servants, the prophets.
The prophets spoke Your words.
They said, “The land you are entering to possess is unclean.
The people of this land are impure.
They have filled the land with abominations.
The land is polluted from one end to the other by their uncleanness.”
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֛ה מַה־ נֹּאמַ֥ר אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ אַֽחֲרֵי־ זֹ֑את כִּ֥י עָזַ֖בְנוּ מִצְוֺתֶֽיךָ׃ אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוִּ֗יתָ בְּיַ֨ד עֲבָדֶ֣יךָ הַנְּבִיאִים֮ לֵאמֹר֒ הָאָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֨ר אַתֶּ֤ם בָּאִים֙ לְרִשְׁתָּ֔הּ אֶ֤רֶץ נִדָּה֙ הִ֔יא בְּנִדַּ֖ת עַמֵּ֣י הָאֲרָצ֑וֹת בְּתוֹעֲבֹֽתֵיהֶ֗ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר מִלְא֛וּהָ מִפֶּ֥ה אֶל־ פֶּ֖ה בְּטֻמְאָתָֽם׃

passages.text: Now, therefore, do not give your daughters in marriage to their sons or take their daughters for your sons. Never seek their peace or prosperity, so that you may be strong and may eat the good things of the land, leaving it as an inheritance to your sons forever.’
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the Israelites through His prophets.
God gave them clear commands about the people of the land.
God said, “Do not give your daughters to their sons in marriage.
Do not take their daughters for your sons.
Do not seek peace with these people.
Do not seek their prosperity.
Do not do this at any time.
If you obey, you will be strong.
You will eat the good things of the land.
You will leave the land as an inheritance for your sons forever.”
passages.original: וְ֠עַתָּה בְּֽנוֹתֵיכֶ֞ם אַל־ תִּתְּנ֣וּ לִבְנֵיהֶ֗ם וּבְנֹֽתֵיהֶם֙ אַל־ תִּשְׂא֣וּ לִבְנֵיכֶ֔ם וְלֹֽא־ תִדְרְשׁ֧וּ שְׁלֹמָ֛ם וְטוֹבָתָ֖ם עַד־ עוֹלָ֑ם לְמַ֣עַן תֶּחֶזְק֗וּ וַאֲכַלְתֶּם֙ אֶת־ ט֣וּב הָאָ֔רֶץ וְהוֹרַשְׁתֶּ֥ם לִבְנֵיכֶ֖ם עַד־ עוֹלָֽם׃

passages.text: After all that has come upon us because of our evil deeds and our great guilt (though You, our God, have punished us less than our iniquities deserve and have given us such a remnant as this), shall we again break Your commandments and intermarry with the peoples who commit these abominations? Would You not become so angry with us as to wipe us out, leaving no remnant or survivor?
passages.sermon:
God, You are our God.
We have done many evil deeds.
We have great guilt.
Many troubles have come upon us because of our sins.
You, God, have not punished us as much as we deserve.
You have shown us mercy.
You have allowed a remnant of us to survive.
You have given us people who remain.
Should we now break Your commandments again?
Should we marry people from these nations who do abominable things?
If we do this, will You not become very angry with us?
Will You not destroy us completely?
Will You not leave us without any remnant or survivor?
passages.original: וְאַֽחֲרֵי֙ כָּל־ הַבָּ֣א עָלֵ֔ינוּ בְּמַעֲשֵׂ֙ינוּ֙ הָרָעִ֔ים וּבְאַשְׁמָתֵ֖נוּ הַגְּדֹלָ֑ה כִּ֣י׀ אַתָּ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ חָשַׂ֤כְתָּֽ לְמַ֙טָּה֙ מֵֽעֲוֺנֵ֔נוּ וְנָתַ֥תָּה לָּ֛נוּ פְּלֵיטָ֖ה כָּזֹֽאת׃ הֲנָשׁוּב֙ לְהָפֵ֣ר מִצְוֺתֶ֔יךָ וּ֨לְהִתְחַתֵּ֔ן בְּעַמֵּ֥י הַתֹּעֵב֖וֹת הָאֵ֑לֶּה הֲל֤וֹא תֶֽאֱנַף־ בָּ֙נוּ֙ עַד־ כַּלֵּ֔ה לְאֵ֥ין שְׁאֵרִ֖ית וּפְלֵיטָֽה׃פ

passages.text: O LORD, God of Israel, You are righteous! For we remain this day as a remnant. Here we are before You in our guilt, though because of it no one can stand before You.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD is righteous.
We are the people of Israel.
We remain today as a remnant.
We stand before You, God, in our guilt.
Because of our guilt, no one can stand before You.
passages.original: יְהוָ֞ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ צַדִּ֣יק אַ֔תָּה כִּֽי־ נִשְׁאַ֥רְנוּ פְלֵיטָ֖ה כְּהַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה הִנְנ֤וּ לְפָנֶ֙יךָ֙ בְּאַשְׁמָתֵ֔ינוּ כִּ֣י אֵ֥ין לַעֲמ֛וֹד לְפָנֶ֖יךָ עַל־ זֹֽאת׃פ
